conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode, sides field says mirrored/same. Helpers: isFirstBarOfSession(n) = bar[n] is the first bar of its trading day/session (date[n] != date[n+1] going backward, i.e. a new session started at bar n); bullTrendBar(n)/bearTrendBar(n) = body(n) fraction test per TrendBarByBody-style primitive.

candidates.name: IsFirstBarOfSession
candidates.quote: Bar 1 on both the Globex chart on the left and on the day session chart on the right is the 6:35 a.m. PST bar.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar is the first bar of the day (intraday) session, i.e. its session date differs from the prior bar's session date. Used to gate opening-bar-only setups.

complexity.reason: requires a session/date-change accessor, not plain OHLC arithmetic

notes: Brooks never states this test explicitly; it is inferred as the structural definition needed for every 'first bar of the day' rule in this and later chapters.

candidates.name: FirstBarTrendContinuationScalp
candidates.quote: Remember that if the first bar of the day is a trend bar, it is usually a setup for a scalp.
candidates.description: If the first bar of the session is a bull trend bar, take a scalp long (mechanized as entry at the next bar's open once the first bar closes as a trend bar).
candidates.pseudocode: (ctx.SessionDate(0) != ctx.SessionDate(1)) && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: stop one tick beyond the first bar's high (long) / low (short)

complexity.reason: combines the session-boundary primitive with a single-bar trend-bar test

notes: 'Usually a setup for a scalp' is Brooks's framing of the exit as a small, fast target rather than a swing; captured here only as the entry.

candidates.name: FirstBarTrendFailureReversal
candidates.quote: If it fails, especially with an opposite trend bar, it is a setup in the opposite direction.
candidates.description: The first bar of the session was a bull trend bar (a failed long setup), and the very next bar is a bear trend bar that closes below the first bar's open: enter short (mechanized at the following bar's open).
candidates.pseudocode: (ctx.SessionDate(1) != ctx.SessionDate(2)) && close[1] > open[1] && (close[1] - open[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1] - low[1]) && close[0] < open[0] && (open[0] - close[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && close[0] < open[1]
candidates.book_order_type: stop one tick beyond the failure bar's low (short) / high (long)

complexity.reason: two-bar pattern anchored on the session-boundary primitive, otherwise fixed-offset comparisons

notes: Brooks does not give a precise 'failure' threshold; using close beyond the first bar's open as the fail test is a reading of 'if it fails'.

candidates.name: OpeningMaUnreliableAfterGap
candidates.quote: Traders who watch only the day session have to be aware that the moving average is often unreliable for the first hour or so.
candidates.description: Context filter: after a large gap that the market is quickly closing, suppress or distrust close-vs-EMA trend classification for roughly the first hour of the session and prefer a momentum reading (e.g. consecutive same-direction closes) instead.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.SessionDate(0) != ctx.SessionDate(1) /* placeholder for 'within N minutes of the open' */ && abs(open[0] - close[largeGapLookback]) >= largeGapTicks * tick

complexity.reason: 'large gap', 'closing it', and 'unreliable for about an hour' are qualitative judgments; a design decision is needed for what replaces the EMA test during that window before this can be coded

notes: This is advice about which indicator to trust, not itself a bar-level entry/exit test; recorded as a filter because it would gate other EMA-based filters.

rejected.quote: The Globex and day session usually give signals at the same time, but often from different patterns... the moving average on the Globex is often in the opposite direction to that in the day session.
rejected.reason: requires a second bar series for the same instrument on a different session (Globex/overnight feed) that a single-session backtest engine does not ingest

rejected.quote: Bar 1 on both the Globex chart on the left and on the day session chart on the right is the 6:35 a.m. PST bar. The Globex had a final flag reversal buy signal, and the day session had a bear trend bar reversal...
rejected.reason: one-off discretionary chart narration tied to a specific figure/time, not a generalizable bar-level test

chapter_summary: Short chapter contrasting the Globex (overnight) and day-session charts and arguing traders should pick one. Only two generalizable mechanizable ideas survive: the first-bar-of-session trend-bar scalp (and its failure-reversal counterpart), and a soft filter that the EMA is unreliable as a trend proxy for roughly the first hour after a large gap. Everything about comparing Globex vs. day-session signals is rejected as needing a second data feed the engine does not have.
